question: In which king’s honour and praise was the Prayag Prashasti written by the Sanskrit poet Harisena?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Samudragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prayag Prashasti, also known as the Allahabad Pillar Inscription, was composed by Harisena, a court poet and minister of Samudragupta.
 
• Samudragupta was a ruler of the Gupta Empire and is often referred to as the "Napoleon of India" due to his extensive military conquests.
 
• The inscription is one of the most important sources of information about the reign of Samudragupta, detailing his conquests and achievements.
 
• It is located on the Allahabad Pillar, which is also known for inscriptions from other historical figures, including Ashoka and Jahangir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta:**

 
 
• Samudragupta was the second ruler of the Gupta Empire, succeeding his father Chandragupta I.
 
• He reigned from approximately 335-375 CE and was known for his military prowess and patronage of the arts.
 
• His rule is often considered a golden age in Indian history due to the flourishing of art, culture, and religion.
 
• He performed the Ashvamedha (horse sacrifice) to signify his undisputed sovereignty over the subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Prayag Prashasti:**
 
 
• The Prayag Prashasti is an eulogy written in classical Sanskrit and is one of the finest examples of ancient Indian inscriptions.
 
• It provides a detailed account of Samudragupta's military campaigns, his administration, and his contributions to the Gupta Empire.
 
• The inscription is valuable not just for its historical content but also for its literary quality, showcasing the high level of Sanskrit literary culture during the Gupta period.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire:**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire was an ancient Indian empire existing from approximately 320 to 550 CE.
 
• It is considered a period of great cultural and scientific advancements, often referred to as the Golden Age of India.
 
• The empire was known for its achievements in science, technology, engineering, art, dialectic, literature, logic, mathematics, astronomy, religion, and philosophy.
